title: Oath and Salt
premise: Zephyrine Blackwood has survived five years as a royal food-taster in Vhalcrest, a city that executes mages, by keeping her small illegal charms hidden and her past buried. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the drowned isles, Zephyrine realizes the girl carries the last living memory of the sea-magic her own family helped destroy. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitor and courted by rebels who want to weaponize the child, Zephyrine must choose between preserving her invented identity and restoring a truth that could reignite the ancient war between land and tide. In the end she surrenders her own memories of safety to seal the child's secret, becoming a stranger to herself but giving the old language a future.
about_author: Orsen Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write about people who carry histories too heavy to hold alone, and live near a cold coast they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine morning tasting for the Queen establishes her careful double life: licensed poison-eater by day, charm-seller by night, magic outlawed on pain of drowning. She swallows a laced broth meant for the Queen and hides the tremor it leaves in her hands. Emotional beat: controlled fear, the cost of belonging to a city that would kill what she is.

chapters.title: A Knock in Low Tide
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. During a storm, a mud-soaked child appears at her door and speaks a single sentence in a language Zephyrine hasn't heard since childhood — the tongue of the drowned isles her mother sang in. The girl cannot or will not speak anything else. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past arriving at the threshold she built to keep it out.

chapters.title: Charms Against Drowning
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She shelters the child, whom she names Brine, and tests her with old charms; Brine's presence makes dead charms glow. Zephyrine realizes the girl is a living vessel of pre-kingdom memory. First glimpse of the Inquisitor Corvane watching her street. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with terror of discovery.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Inquisitor interrogates Zephyrine over tea, courteous and surgical, revealing he knows someone sold charms in the Saltmarket and that a 'tide-child' was seen. He offers protection in exchange for information. Zephyrine lies well, but not perfectly. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse dread; power disguised as politeness.

chapters.title: What the Rebels Want
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The charm network's leader, an ex-priest named Odell, reveals the rebels know about Brine and want her as a symbol to rally the outlawed faithful — or a weapon against the Crown. Zephyrine refuses, making an enemy of her only allies. Emotional beat: the loneliness of refusing every side.

chapters.title: Memory of Water
chapters.summary: Brine's POV, rendered in fragmented sensory prose. Through touch, Brine shares visions with Zephyrine: the drowning of the isles, mages walking into the sea rather than burn, and a woman with Zephyrine's face among them. Zephyrine learns her family didn't just survive the purge — they helped betray it. Emotional beat: grief and shame rewriting identity.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Corvane raids the Saltmarket; Odell is taken, and under questioning gives up Zephyrine's name. She flees with Brine through the flooded undercity, using her mother's forbidden tide-craft openly for the first time. Emotional beat: liberation and exposure — she cannot go back to being no one.

chapters.title: The Drowned Court
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Following Brine's leading, they reach a sunken temple where the last sea-mages' memories pool like light in water. There Zephyrine learns the truth: the war never ended, it only sleeps, and Brine's memory is the key both sides will kill to hold or erase. Corvane arrives with soldiers. Emotional beat: cornered clarity.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Climax, Zephyrine's POV. In the temple, Corvane demands Brine; the rebels arrive demanding her too. Zephyrine performs the rite her ancestors perverted — offering her own memories of safety, home, and self as payment to seal Brine's secret beyond reach. Corvane, glimpsing what she sacrifices, lets them go. Emotional beat: devastating choice made freely.

chapters.title: Oath and Salt
chapters.summary: Brine's POV, then Zephyrine's. Months later, Zephyrine remembers nothing of why she keeps a quiet girl she calls her niece, only that she swore an oath she can't recall and feels peace she doesn't trust. Brine, now speaking softly in two tongues, guards the story for both of them. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity surrendered so that belonging, for someone else, could survive.
